articleTitle: Coupling coefficients of irregular microstrip resonators and selective properties of filters on their basis
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Frequency-dependent coefficients of coupling between irregular microstrip resonators and their role in the formation of a filter's frequency response are studied on the basis of an energetic approach. Two-resonator segments and filters are used as the samples under investigation. A theoretical analysis carried out in the quasi-static approximation shows good agreement between calculated and experimental frequency responses and, thus, allows us to conclude that the attenuation poles in the frequency response are due to compensation of the capacitive and inductive interaction between resonators. The data obtained show the possibility of controlling the steepness of filter skirt slopes by appropriate choice of structural parameters.

articleTitle: MW energy irradiator for reflexotherapy
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The efficiency of MW power transmission from the end of a coaxial waveguide to a biologically active point (BAP) is considered. The distribution of the power in biological tissue (BT) irradiated by UHF electromagnetic radiation when the end of the coaxial irradiator is in close contact with the surface of the BAP is measured. It is shown that under such conditions 50% of the irradiated power is absorbed in a BT layer of thickness 0.5 mm and 90% in a 1 mm layer.

articleTitle: Throughput efficiency of the modified SR algorithm [ARQ]
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: To increase the throughput efficiency of SR algorithm, it is recommended to use the modified SR (MSR) algorithm using error controlling code (ECC) with correction of low number of errors. The MSR effectiveness evaluation is made in the paper.

articleTitle: A model of the shielded multiconductor microstrip lines on double-layer substrate - a novel approach
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The shielded multiconductor microstrip lines on double-layer substrate are analyzed by using a novel analytical algorithm, which combines the method of subregions with perfect boundaries and the conformal mapping technique. Examples of numerical modeling of some structures are presented. The results of application of these novel method have shown high efficiency in computation speed and good accuracy.

articleTitle: Field analysis (full-wave) of millimeter-wave HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: In this paper an efficient method for full-wave analysis of millimeter-wave HEMTs is presented. The effect of wave propagation on transistor's structure is considered using finite difference time domain (FDTD) method (full-wave analysis). The active properties of transistor are studied using a small signal current density coupled to Maxwell's equations. This method provides simulation time reduction and can be applied to the next generation of simulators for simultaneous electromagnetic-electronic modelling of mm-wave devices.

articleTitle: Design features for polysilicon high pressure transducers
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: In this experimental work, polysilicon pressure transducers are designed with pressure-sensitive elements and applied for pressure over 5 MPa. To determine the magnitude of mechanical stress in the diaphragm, we defined gauge factors from longitudinal and transverse piezoresistors on console beam made from the same wafer as the diaphragm. Also, we modeled mechanical stress in the diaphragm by the finite element method (FEM) by taking into account not only the uniformly distributed load on the plate of diaphragm, but also the load on the lateral side of the diaphragm. The comparison of the calculated mechanical stress with the experimentally defined stress has shown a coincidence within 20% error bound.

articleTitle: The tracking algorithm and processor for smart antenna cellular communications
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The tracking RLS algorithm with low computational complexity for application in cellular communication smart antenna processor that allows one to decrease the cost of the base station is presented. The proposed implementation of the algorithm has higher performance than conventional RLS algorithm because it requires only vector operation and has a regular structure. We present the software and hardware implementation of the proposed algorithm and comparison of computational complexity and convergence with conventional RLS algorithm.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic processes in the multilayer circular cut-off waveguides
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The results of the investigation of wave processes in circular waveguides with inhomogeneous dielectric filling are presented. Physical reasons for the high sensitivity of the propagation constants to the change in material parameters of the structure are considered. It is shown that in the off-limit frequency region the waveguides exhibit new properties. On the basis of these properties transducers for the measuring of electro-physical characteristics of different materials and fluid media can be developed.

articleTitle: Waveguide-to-coaxial transition of reduced height
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The results of the waveguide-to-coaxial transition design based on the finite element method (FEM) are considered in this paper. The special features of this transition are the reduced height and the complex structure of its construction. The calculation of this transition parameter is difficult because of the nonstandard cross-section of the waveguide and the high value of the exiting post longitude. The finite element method should be most effective in calculating waveguide-to-coaxial transition. It allows one to design waveguide-to-coaxial transitions of classical construction and original construction (for instance with dielectric filling) which are divided into a large quantity of small regions and to calculate the field in each element of the mesh.

articleTitle: The analysis of one protocol of short message transmission over the discrete channel, described by Hilbert model
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Discrete radio channel, as shown by numerous studies is completely described by Hilbert model. The approximation of experimental data, obtained in DECT system radio channel by Hilbert model taking into account double return to bad state, was shown. In this work, a formula was calculated to find the probability of m-divisible errors in the block of n-element length. We use these results to analyze one of the short message delivery protocols in radio channel, described by Hilbert model.

articleTitle: The lumped resonant elements in waveguides
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Traditionally waveguide filters are constructed using a limited amount of resonant elements. The volumetric cascade resonators or resonant diaphragms are applied as passing circuits. Rejection circuits are usually implemented as series stubs. The expansion of the nomenclature of resonant elements allows us to reduce considerably the dimensions of devices and to improve their electrical parameters. In this paper we consider resonant elements having a small longitudinal (along the waveguide) dimension that allows us in most cases to consider them as lumped.

articleTitle: Thin-film comb thermal converter: Influence of design parameters on high-frequency currents distribution
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Thin-film comb thermal converters are widely used in state-of-the-art measurement instrumentation for obtaining mean-square root values of ac current or voltage and for measuring power of signals having arbitrary shapes and bandwidth. These converters offer a number of advantages compared to bulk thermal converters: high volt-watt sensitivity, small size, high reproducibility of characteristics. The paper presents analytical dependencies of the high-frequency current distribution in the thin-film thermal converter on its design parameters and operating frequency.

articleTitle: The broadband SSB upconverter with wide dynamic range
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Multiple 90/spl deg/ couplers, 180/spl deg/- and 0/spl deg/- dividers together with balanced mixers are combined to create a new type of SSB upconverter. Such an upconverter has the following features: (1) wide dynamic range; (2) a high sideband suppression degree; (3) low VSWR at all ports; (4) low conversion loss; and (5) high carrier rejection. The paper describes the operation of the SSB upconverter developed for radio transmitting applications.

articleTitle: Synthesis and analysis architecture and operation of echo-compensator based on channel relative characteristics
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: A second-order echo-compensator operating algorithm and device architecture have been developed using channel relative properties. The analysis has shown that the main technical performances exceeds those of known algorithms.

articleTitle: High-power microwave semiconductor controlling devices
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: In the present work a symmetric distributed structure included powerful switching diodes is considered. The wave impedance transformation of the microwave tract and the input reflection factor value close to one, providing outside the band of working frequencies, allows us to expand essentially the band of working frequencies. The developed technique of calculation can be used for designing various microwave control devices.

articleTitle: Broadband microwave attenuator
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: In the present work the effective circuit designs of centimeter range microwave attenuators based on p-i-n diodes are considered. The offered strip line structures ensure operation in a wide band of frequencies and small level of direct losses.

articleTitle: Correlation-spectral 2-D ISAR image reconstruction from linear frequency modulation signals
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The developed correlation-spectral 2-D ISAR image reconstruction method can be applied over ISAR time data. The procedure is invariant of trajectory parameters of an observed object. The boundary conditions for utilizing ISAR image reconstruction procedures invariant to trajectory parameters of an object are defined. The azimuth resolution of an object image is very sensitive to variation of ISAR parameters that have to be adjusted in any concrete case defined in accordance with a range distance to the target.

articleTitle: Throughput efficiency of automatic repeat request algorithm with selective reject in communication links with large signal propagation delay
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: In this paper, the efficiency of automatic repeat request (ARQ) algorithm with selective reject (SR) in communication links with large signal propagation delay (GSPD), such as microwave satellite communication links, is measured in terms of throughput. The throughput dependence of pure SR algorithm on code block length n is considered for some channel conditions. Recommendations on evaluation of optimal n and implementation of received results in GSPD channel applications are stated.

articleTitle: Amplitude versus frequency response characteristic correction of band pass filters with losses
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: This work is devoted to the development of an iterative method for the amplitude correction versus frequency response characteristic peak form of band-pass filters with dissipated losses. The offered technique ensures minimum magnitude of initial damping in the whole band of working frequencies.

articleTitle: About the step-down transformer on lines
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: We previously reported about the step-down transformer on two pieces of lines. The transformer can be designed with the ratio of voltage or resistance transformation proportional both to whole number and to fractions. The same step-down transformer can be designed from three pieces of lines.

articleTitle: A measurement method of microwave network parameters by multiport analyzers
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The complex reflection coefficient measurement by a multiport network analyzer with high precision and calibration precision control is presented. The authors consider a measurement method which permits one, under certain conditions, to make a calibration on one input as well as measurement on other input thus enabling the measurement in a compatible frequency band of the parameters of devices with different types of connectors.

articleTitle: Multiple-stage combline bandpass filter made of /spl lambda//4 transmission line resonators
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: A new design method is proposed for multiple-stage combline bandpass filter made of transmission line resonators. The Grayzel transformation is used for separating the two adjacent couplings of each resonator and decomposing the filter into a parallel connection of two coupled resonators. After the design is finished, identical resonators are equally spaced with auxiliary capacitors, which is the simplest structure to fabricate.

articleTitle: Thyristor based thermoregulator for technological ovens
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: In this paper the design of the precise thermoregulator for high temperature ovens is described. The electrical circuitry is based on thyristors to fulfill the main requirements: wide range of regulation, accuracy of control and electromagnetic compatibility. For practical purposes the pulse method and microprocessor controller are used. The results of the experiments and the advantage of the circuitry are discussed.

articleTitle: Valid error estimation for complex permittivity measurements using partially filled microwave resonators
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Suggests an approach to evaluate the error of complex permittivity in dielectric measurements using partially filled microwave resonators. The approach uses the characteristic equation obtained by field matching technique and has no limitation associated with a value of complex permittivity under test. Using experimental data the comparison of the measurement error evaluated by the approach presented to error followed from formulas based on simple perturbation theory is carried out for a number of dielectrics. The comparison shows that these two estimations may be essentially different. The approach presented may be also applied to dielectric measurements using resonators with complex shape and complex dielectric filling when the characteristic equation is obtained by the field matching technique.

articleTitle: EHF autodyne signals for tracking the parameters of moving objects
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: To improve the characteristics of short-range autodyne radar systems and to extend their application range, it is very important from both theoretical and practical viewpoints to study the autodyne signal waveform and spectrum. In the present paper, the results of investigations into the specific features of the autodyne response of an EHF generator are presented as functions of the parameters of a moving object and the radiation reflectance. The results of experiments performed in the present work are in agreement with theoretical conclusions.

articleTitle: Analysis of active microwave filter using dual-mode dielectric resonators
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Compensation of insertion losses of a dual-mode waveguide-dielectric microwave filter using Gunn diodes as active device is investigated. The field model of a Gunn diode is introduced. Some experimental data concerning an active dual-mode microwave filter are reported.

articleTitle: Direct reconstructing voltage-current distribution in arbitrary nonuniform transmission line
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Reconstructing voltage-current distribution in an arbitrary nonuniform transmission line is presented on the basis of the direct solution of the generalized telegraphic equation with a proper boundary condition. The details of the reconstructing procedure are also given. Wronskian determinant behavior is used to estimate the accuracy of the reconstruction process.

articleTitle: High-resistance thick silicon epitaxial layers
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The development and introduction of powerful high-voltage diodes and transistors, p-i-n diodes, photodiodes, avalanche diodes and other devices require silicon epitaxial layers with high resistance and large thickness, smooth surfaces and a considerable extent of crystallographic perfection, i.e. a minimal number of structural defects. CVD appears to be the most suitable technology for obtaining such layers.

articleTitle: Two-stage non-linear algorithm of the piecewise constant image filtration
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The task of stepwise random field filtering which is observed on a background of additive Gaussian white noise is considered. For the assumed model, recurrent relationships for calculation of two-dimensional a posteriori distribution of useful and control signal probabilities are found. It is shown that the filtering mean-square error for the obtained non-causal algorithm is much less than that for a causal one.

articleTitle: Method of two-direction signal division operating on nonlinear communication channels
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Relative compensation method of the third order (RCM-3) for operation on nonlinear communication channels has been designed and explored. The structure of echo-compensator (RCM-3) design is given and the main technical characteristics are calculated.

articleTitle: Microwave/RF sensors for composition control of continuous flows
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Results of numerical investigation of complex propagation constants in circular multilayer waveguides are presented. A model is based on the characteristic equation given in algorithmic manner and can yield the complete spectrum of the waveguides in question. As a result of the investigation, a novel type of RF/microwave evanescent mode sensor is suggested. These sensors can be used for composition control of continuous flows and have been applied for composition control of oil flows in well pipes.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of the balanced diode frequency multiplier on coupled transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The model of the balanced frequency multiplier on coupled transmission lines is considered. This is characterized by simplicity, and high qualitative parameters. The computation sequence based on decomposition of the circuit on linear and nonlinear parts is given and this allows one to simplify a design technique.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of microwave high-power microstrip loads
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Mathematical model of microstrip transmission line with losses used as a final load or a high-power attenuator is developed. The model is based on the decomposition impedance approach. The equivalent circuit, which represents impedance analog of the load, is obtained by partitioning the resistance stratum surface on a two-dimensional grid from elementary blocks. The division of the blocks in the cross-section involves current heterogeneity of the microstrip transmission line. The connection between elementary blocks in the cross-section is described by means of cross-inductive method. It ensures galvanic outcome of resistors which are used to describe dispersion of microwave power, and allows one to define precisely an input impedance on zero frequency. The developed model can be used on frequencies from 0 up to 20 GHz for high-power loads having significant longitudinal and transversal sizes.

articleTitle: Coupling factors of regular microstrip resonators
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: In quasi-static approximation the coupling factors of regular microstrip resonators were investigated. The regularities of coupling factor behavior caused by changing the design data of interacting resonators connected to external transmission lines by long and by short diagonals were investigated. It is theoretically and experimentally shown, that at frequencies of the second passband the given coupling factor can be realized at three various spacings between resonators.

articleTitle: Selective properties of microstrip filters based on hairpin resonators with stub elements
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: Using a quasi-static approximation, the selective properties of two-resonator filters based on hairpin resonators with irregular stub elements are investigated. The obtained results and good agreement between the theory and experiment allow us to determine the conductor pattern of a filter with given performance using parametrical synthesis. The possibility of increasing significantly the selectivity of microstrip filters by means of cascade connecting two-resonator sections through a chip amplifier is shown.

articleTitle: The mathematical model of the multilayer circular waveguides
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The special features of dielectrometry monitoring of heterogeneous materials and medium are discussed. An electrodynamical model for a primary measuring converter in circular waveguides are considered. The results of investigation of the characteristics of a regular circular waveguide with a discrete layered filler are presented. The presented results may be used for measuring electrophysical parameters of materials and for monitoring the constituent elements of a fluid medium.

articleTitle: Using of GIS EHF autodyne transceiver modules on mesa-planar Gunn diodes for definition of turbomachine blades deformations
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The levels of mechanical deformations of dynamically loaded blades in modern turbomachines to a great extent define the durability and reliability of gas-turbine engines (GTEs). The authors present a radar method and device for the control of dynamic blades characteristics of a GTE. The block diagram of the measuring stand and results of experimental studies are given.

articleTitle: Comparison of noise properties of various microwave active filters
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: In this paper, five topologies of microwave active filters (MAFs) are studied. We have considered MAFs proposed earlier in the class of filters with compensation for loss. First we have investigated theoretically the noise properties of various approaches to compensate for losses in microwave resonators. Then five third order microstrip active filters were simulated to validate a choice of the best configuration. It was shown that the use of negative resistance with minimized noise measure gives a reduced noise figure under the same conditions.

articleTitle: The waveguide transformer on the lumped elements
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: A method of calculation and design of a waveguide transformer based on lumped elements having small dimensions is described.

articleTitle: Waveguide band-pass filters on the lumped elements
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: For the synthesis of waveguide filters the ladder structure is accepted as an initial prototype. In this paper the calculation and design methods of a waveguide bandpass filter constructed using a ladder circuit based on lumped elements, are described.

articleTitle: Account and experimental researches of strain in square diaphragm [pressure sensors]
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The task of analysing the large deflections in a square diaphragm is solved. The analytical expressions for presence of deflections in a square diaphragm are assessed in view of deformation of the middle of a plane. The simple algorithms of defining a component tensor of strain are given. Good agreement between experimental and analytical results for the diaphragm are demonstrated. Nonlinear strain and relative changes of resistance of longitudinal and cross resistors on a diaphragm are calculated.

articleTitle: Influence of method of excitation on the characteristics of low pressure plasma high frequency discharge
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The influence of a technique of excitation of HF discharge on size of power density in plasma is investigated. The following variants of excitation of the discharge are considered: the high frequency induction discharge (HFID), electrodeless HF capacitor discharge (EHFCD) and mixed variant HFI-EHFC with variable capacity of the discharge.

articleTitle: Investigation of semiconductor structures and two-dimensional systems by non-destructive contactless methods
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: In this paper the investigation of semiconductors by the high-frequency, magneto-optical and microwave methods is presented. These methods are based on the observation of the oscillation and resonance effects in semiconductors. The experimental data of determining transport and energy parameters of structures obtained in the observation of the Shubnikov-de Haas effect and nonlinear spin resonance due to stimulated combinational light scattering method with the signal amplification are considered.

articleTitle: Image decorrelation based on the representation by stochastic models
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: In a number of cases many of the image processing tasks require decorrelation, which simplifies or makes possible subsequent processing. The decorrelation technique based on image representation by causal and non-causal stochastic models is proposed. The influence of the procedure both on background, and on the information component of the image is considered. The results of processing by rank detector operating on decorrelated preparation in the task of step edge detection are given.

articleTitle: Allocation of frequencies in a network of terrestrial digital audio broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The method for allocation of frequencies in a network of terrestrial digital audio broadcasting is developed. The defined frequency-distance of constraint and the optimal value of a step of frequencies are calculated. In the realization used the authors offered a universal model of a homogeneous network and method of coordination rings.

articleTitle: Development of a method of harmonic balance for multi-periodic solutions of the nonlinear equations
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The problems of implementation of the harmonic balance (HB) method for multi-periodic effects are discussed. The algorithms of optimization of fundamental frequencies set of the HB method, permitting one to reduce its number, are offered which promotes a diminution of HB set of equations size and realize the most effective HB algorithm. A new approach to the solution of the HB set of equations is offered, which allows one to exclude errors of spectrums superposition at commensurable fundamental frequencies. The effective algorithm of numerical calculation of the HB Jacobian matrix for multi-periodic effects is offered.

articleTitle: Small-signal and large-signal noise analyses of nonlinear circuits in frequency domain
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The problems of a noise analysis of nonlinear circuits for small and large signal levels are surveyed. It is shown, that the known method of correlation analysis of linear circuits requiring knowledge of the correlation matrices of all elements of the circuit can be implemented at a level of primary sources of noises of each circuit element. Such an approach essentially simplifies a mathematical and algorithmic realization of the analysis, dilating its possibilities on all devices, for which the equivalent noise circuits are known but the correlation noise matrix is not obtained. The nonlinear analysis of nonlinear circuit noise is discussed. The method of nonlinear noise analysis based on canonical decomposition of spectral densities of the circuit's noise sources is presented. The method, contrary to the LSSS method, widely used in the programs for the nonlinear analysis of microwave and RF circuits, allows effectively to parse both poorly "rustling" circuits, and circuit with a very high noise level, when the nonlinearity of the circuit in relation to noise cannot be neglected.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: 2001 Microwave Electronics: Measurement, Identification, Applications. Conference Proceedings. MEMIA'2001 (Cat. No.01EX474)
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.
